name: STACKIT Workflows DAG Run Intermediate Catch Event Connector
description: Waits until a STACKIT Workflows DAG run is finished (success or failed) and continues with the run as payload. Polls the Airflow API of the instance on the process's behalf. Same prerequisites as the STACKIT Workflows outbound connector: an OAuth2 identity provider with an API Audience on the instance and a client with the Airflow role User.

groups.label: Correlation
groups.tooltip: Learn more about message correlation in the documentation.

properties.label: Token URL
properties.description: The token endpoint of the identity provider configured on the Workflows instance, for example https://keycloak.example.com/realms/airflow/protocol/openid-connect/token. Must use https.

properties.label: Client ID
properties.description: A client in that identity provider allowed to use the client_credentials grant, for example {{secrets.STACKIT_WORKFLOWS_CLIENT_ID}}. Not a STACKIT service account.

properties.label: Client secret
properties.description: Store it as a Camunda secret and reference it, for example {{secrets.STACKIT_WORKFLOWS_CLIENT_SECRET}}.

properties.label: Scope
properties.description: Optional, space-separated. Entra ID needs the application ID URI of the API with /.default, for example api://my-airflow-api/.default.

properties.label: Audience
properties.description: Optional audience parameter for identity providers that take one (Okta, Auth0). The token's aud claim must match the API Audience configured on the instance, however the identity provider sets it.

properties.label: Resource
properties.description: Optional RFC 8707 resource parameter. Leave empty unless your identity provider requires it.

properties.label: Client authentication
properties.description: How the client ID and secret are sent to the token endpoint. Use the method the client is configured for in the identity provider.

properties.label: Instance URL
properties.description: The URL of the STACKIT Workflows instance, as shown in the STACKIT Portal (the Airflow UI URL). Without /api/v1 or /api/v2. Must use https.

properties.label: Airflow API version
properties.description: v1 for Airflow 2.11 instances (workflows-2.3-airflow-2.11, /api/v1), v2 for Airflow 3.1 instances (workflows-3.0-airflow-3.1, /api/v2). The connector does not detect the version; a wrong value fails with NOT_FOUND.

pattern.message: must be v1 (Airflow 2.11), v2 (Airflow 3.1), a FEEL expression or a secret reference

properties.label: DAG ID
properties.description: The dag_id of the DAG, for example =exportDagId.

properties.label: Run ID
properties.description: The run to wait for, evaluated per waiting process instance: typically the dagRunId returned by Trigger DAG run, for example =exportRunId. Use the same expression as the correlation key below.

properties.label: Polling interval
properties.description: How often the state of every waiting run is read, an ISO 8601 duration of at least PT5S, for example PT30S or PT5M. One Airflow API call per waiting process instance and interval.

pattern.message: must be an ISO 8601 duration such as PT30S

properties.label: Activation condition
properties.description: Condition under which the Connector triggers. Leave empty to catch all events

properties.label: Correlation key (process)
properties.description: Sets up the correlation key from process variables

properties.label: Correlation key (payload)
properties.description: Extracts the correlation key from the incoming message payload

properties.label: Message ID expression
properties.description: Expression to extract unique identifier of a message

properties.label: Message TTL
properties.description: Time-to-live for the message in the broker (ISO-8601 duration)

properties.label: Message name
properties.tooltip: By default, this is an auto-generated random UUID. We recommend using a unique message name for each connector element in the diagram. Override to set a custom message name. Learn more about message subscriptions that power inbound connectors.

properties.label: Result variable
properties.description: Name of variable to store the response in. Details in the documentation.

properties.label: Result expression
properties.description: Expression to map the response into process variables. Details in the documentation.
